{"body":"## Summary

Fix dropped checkpoints when Claude Code runs from inside its `.claude/worktrees/<branch>/` feature. Three independent issues conspired to make agent work in linked worktrees invisible to Entire — fixing only one wasn't enough. This PR addresses all three.

The user-visible symptom: a Claude session that does work in a linked worktree finishes cleanly, but the commit lands without an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, no metadata appears on `entire/checkpoints/v1`, and `entire status` from inside the worktree reports `not set up`.

## What was wrong

**1. Transcript path mismatch.** Claude Code reports `transcript_path` encoded from the worktree CWD, e.g. `~/.claude/projects/-Users-foo-Development-repo--claude-worktrees-feature/<id>.jsonl`, but the file is actually written under the parent repo's project dir at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-foo-Development-repo/<id>.jsonl`. The TurnEnd handler aborted at the file-exists check, so no shadow-branch commit was created.

**2. `.entire/` resolved against the wrong root.** `paths.AbsPath(".entire/settings.json")` used `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, which from inside a linked worktree returns the worktree dir — not the main repo where `.entire/` actually lives. Every git hook firing from inside a linked worktree saw `IsSetUpAndEnabled = false` and silently bailed. `entire status` from the worktree reported `not set up`.

**3. Session matching was strict-equal on `WorktreePath`.** Even with the gate unblocked, `findSessionsForWorktree` couldn't find the active session: `UserPromptSubmit` fired from the main worktree (so the session's `WorktreePath` is the main repo), but `prepare-commit-msg` / `post-commit` fire from inside the linked worktree where the commit happens. Strict equality returned no matches, and hooks logged `no active sessions` at DEBUG and bailed.

## Resolution

**Transcript fallback** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/lifecycle.go`).
When the reported path doesn't exist, the resolver strips the trailing `--claude-worktrees-<branch>` marker from the project segment and stats the parent-repo candidate. Deterministic — no directory scanning, no chance of crossing into an unrelated project that happens to share a session ID. `strings.LastIndex` is used (not `Index`) so repos whose sanitized root already contains the token (e.g. checked out under `acme--claude-worktrees-tools/`) only have the trailing synthetic marker stripped. Gates: triggers only on `os.IsNotExist`, only when the reported path is under `~/.claude/projects/`, only when the project segment carries the marker; session ID validated before `filepath.Join`; candidate must exist before being returned.

**`.entire/` anchored at the main worktree** (`cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go`, `cmd/entire/cli/logging/logger.go`).
New `paths.MainWorktreeRoot` derives the main repo root from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`'s parent. `paths.AbsPath` now routes any `.entire/*` relative path through it; all other paths still resolve against `WorktreeRoot`. `logging.Init` likewise uses `MainWorktreeRoot` so hook log output writes to the canonical `.entire/logs/entire.log` instead of spawning an orphan `.entire/logs/` inside each linked worktree.

**Session lookup widens linked → main** (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_session.go`).
`findSessionsForWorktree` now also accepts sessions whose `WorktreePath` is the main worktree when invoked from a linked worktree. The widening is one-directional — sibling linked worktrees still don't bleed into each other, and main-worktree lookups are unchanged — so commits on main can't accidentally pick up an unrelated agent session running in `.claude/worktrees/<branch>`.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run fmt && mise run lint` — clean
- [x] `mise run test:ci` — unit + integration + canary green
- [x] Transcript resolver unit tests: passthrough, empty inputs, no-marker, marker-at-start, marker-in-repo-root, outside-base, traversal rejection, worktree fallback
- [x] `TestClaudeCode_WorktreePathFallback` (integration): drives `entire hooks claude-code stop` with a fake `HOME` and a worktree-encoded `transcript_path` that doesn't exist; verifies a checkpoint is created end-to-end
- [x] `TestMainWorktreeRoot_LinkedWorktree`, `TestAbsPath_EntireAnchoredAtMainWorktree`, `TestIsEntireRelPath`: path resolution from inside a linked worktree
- [x] `TestLinkedWorktree_EntireSetUpVisible` (integration): `entire status` from a linked worktree reports the active configuration instead of `not set up`
- [x] `TestFindSessionsForWorktree_LinkedWorktreeMatchesMain` / `_MainWorktreeUnchanged`: widening is one-directional
- [x] End-to-end: built binary, ran `entire status` from inside `/path/to/repo/.claude/worktrees/<branch>` and from real prepare-commit-msg invocation; verified hook now logs `prepare-commit-msg hook invoked` and reaches the session-matching layer

## Notes

- Should also be reported upstream to Claude Code: `transcript_path` should match the file's actual storage location.
- The inner Claude session created by Claude's worktrees feature still doesn't fire its own `UserPromptSubmit` because the linked worktree has no `.claude/settings.json` (only `settings.local.json` with permissions). Commits from inside the worktree therefore link to the outer session, not a dedicated sub-session. That's a separate ergonomic limitation upstream of this PR — either Claude needs to carry project hooks into worktrees, or Entire needs to install hooks at `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- The resolver and the session-lookup widening both log at INFO when they take the worktree path (`agent.claudecode resolved transcript via worktree fallback`), observable in `.entire/logs/`.","number":1159,"title":"Recognize agent worktrees in transcript, settings, and session lookup","url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1159"}

237	// IsSubpath reports whether child is lexically under parent (or equal to it).
238	// It uses filepath.Rel, which cleans both inputs and is traversal-resistant:
239	// a crafted child like "/a/b/../../../etc/passwd" that escapes parent will
240	// produce a relative path starting with ".." and be rejected.
241	func IsSubpath(parent, child string) bool {
242		rel, err := filepath.Rel(parent, child)
243		if err != nil {
244			return false

249	// ToRelativePath converts an absolute path to relative.
250	// Returns empty string if the path is outside the working directory.
251	func ToRelativePath(absPath, cwd string) string {
252		absPath = normalizeMSYSPath(absPath)
253		cwd = normalizeMSYSPath(cwd)
254	
255		// On Windows, MSYS/Git Bash sometimes omits the drive letter, producing
256		// paths like /Users/... that filepath.IsAbs doesn't recognize. Prepend
257		// the drive letter from cwd so filepath.Rel can match them.
258		if runtime.GOOS == osWindows && len(absPath) > 0 && absPath[0] == '/' && len(cwd) >= 2 && cwd[1] == ':' {
259			absPath = cwd[:2] + absPath
260		}
261	
262		if !filepath.IsAbs(absPath) {
263			return absPath
264		}
265		relPath, err := filepath.Rel(cwd, absPath)
266		if err != nil || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, "..") {
267			return ""
268		}
269	
270		return relPath
271	}

273	// normalizeMSYSPath converts MSYS/Git Bash-style paths (e.g., /c/Users/...)
274	// to Windows-style paths (e.g., C:/Users/...) so that filepath.IsAbs and
275	// filepath.Rel work correctly. On non-Windows platforms this is a no-op.
276	// Claude Code on Windows outputs MSYS paths in its transcript, but Go's
277	// filepath package only recognizes Windows-style absolute paths.
278	func normalizeMSYSPath(p string) string {
279		if runtime.GOOS != osWindows {
280			return p
281		}
282		// MSYS paths look like /c/Users/... where the second char is a drive letter
283		if len(p) >= 3 && p[0] == '/' && unicode.IsLetter(rune(p[1])) && p[2] == '/' {
284			return string(unicode.ToUpper(rune(p[1]))) + ":" + p[2:]
285		}
286		return p
287	}

292	// SanitizePathForClaude converts a path to Claude's project directory format.
293	// Claude replaces any non-alphanumeric character with a dash.
294	func SanitizePathForClaude(path string) string {
295		return nonAlphanumericRegex.ReplaceAllString(path, "-")

299	// for the given repository path.

302	func GetClaudeProjectDir(repoPath string) (string, error) {
303		override := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR")

308		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()

311		}
312	
313		projectDir := SanitizePathForClaude(repoPath)

318	// for the given Entire session ID. The sessionID must be the full, already date-prefixed
319	// Entire session identifier as stored on disk, not an agent-specific or raw Claude ID.
320	func SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID string) string {
321		return EntireMetadataDir + "/" + sessionID

324	// ExtractSessionIDFromTranscriptPath attempts to extract a session ID from a transcript path.
325	// Claude transcripts are stored at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/sessions/<id>.jsonl
326	// If the path doesn't match expected format, returns empty string.
327	func ExtractSessionIDFromTranscriptPath(transcriptPath string) string {
328		// Try to extract from typical path: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/sessions/<id>.jsonl
329		parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(transcriptPath), "/")
330		for i, part := range parts {
331			if part == "sessions" && i+1 < len(parts) {
332				// Return filename without extension
333				filename := parts[i+1]
334				if strings.HasSuffix(filename, ".jsonl") {
335					return strings.TrimSuffix(filename, ".jsonl")
336				}
337				return filename
338			}
339		}
340		return ""
341	}

191	// claudeWorktreeMarker is the substring that appears in an encoded project-dir
192	// segment when Claude Code is invoked from inside its worktree feature.
193	// SanitizePathForClaude replaces every non-alphanumeric character with '-',
194	// so a CWD ending in "/.claude/worktrees/<branch>" produces a project segment
195	// containing "--claude-worktrees-<branch-encoded>".
196	const claudeWorktreeMarker = "--claude-worktrees-"
197	
198	// resolveTranscriptPath returns the canonical path to a Claude transcript file,
199	// recovering from the Claude Code worktree-feature mismatch where
200	// transcript_path encodes the worktree CWD (e.g. .claude/worktrees/<branch>) but
201	// the file is stored under the parent repo's project dir.
202	//
203	// When the reported path doesn't exist, the resolver strips the worktree marker
204	// from the project segment and checks the parent-repo candidate. The lookup is
205	// fully deterministic — no directory scanning, no chance of crossing into an
206	// unrelated project that happens to share a session ID.
207	//
208	// The fallback is gated to keep risk minimal:
209	//   - Only triggers on os.IsNotExist (permission/IO errors are returned as-is
210	//     so real problems aren't masked).
211	//   - Only triggers when the reported path is under the Claude projects base
212	//     dir.
213	//   - Only triggers when the project segment contains claudeWorktreeMarker.
214	//   - The session ID is validated with validation.ValidateAgentSessionID
215	//     before being used in filepath.Join, blocking traversal via hostile hook
216	//     input.
217	//   - The candidate path must itself exist before being returned.
218	func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) resolveTranscriptPath(sessionRef, sessionID string) string {
219		if sessionRef == "" || sessionID == "" {
220			return sessionRef
221		}
222		if _, err := os.Stat(sessionRef); err == nil {
223			return sessionRef
224		} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
225			return sessionRef
226		}
227		if err := validation.ValidateAgentSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
228			return sessionRef
229		}
230		base, err := c.GetSessionBaseDir()
231		if err != nil {
232			return sessionRef
233		}
234		candidate := worktreeParentCandidate(filepath.Clean(base), filepath.Clean(sessionRef), sessionID)
235		if candidate == "" {
236			return sessionRef
237		}
238		if _, err := os.Stat(candidate); err != nil {
239			return sessionRef
240		}
241		logging.Info(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "agent.claudecode"),
242			"resolved transcript via worktree fallback",
243			slog.String("reported", sessionRef),
244			slog.String("found", candidate),
245			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
246		)
247		return candidate
248	}

250	// worktreeParentCandidate returns the parent-repo equivalent of a reported
251	// transcript path when the project segment carries the Claude Code worktree
252	// marker. Returns "" if reported is not under base, has no project segment,
253	// or has no worktree marker. Callers must validate sessionID before calling.
254	//
255	// strings.LastIndex (not Index) is used because the *synthetic* worktree
256	// marker is always the trailing occurrence in the project segment: Claude
257	// appends "/.claude/worktrees/<branch>" to the cwd, and SanitizePathForClaude
258	// preserves left-to-right order, so the suffix carrying the bug is the last
259	// one. Cutting at the first match would mis-strip repos whose sanitized root
260	// already contains the token (e.g. repos checked out under a directory
261	// literally named "...--claude-worktrees-...").
262	func worktreeParentCandidate(base, reported, sessionID string) string {
263		sep := string(os.PathSeparator)
264		prefix := base + sep
265		if !strings.HasPrefix(reported, prefix) {
266			return ""
267		}
268		projectSeg, _, ok := strings.Cut(reported[len(prefix):], sep)
269		if !ok || projectSeg == "" {
270			return ""
271		}
272		idx := strings.LastIndex(projectSeg, claudeWorktreeMarker)
273		if idx <= 0 {
274			return ""
275		}
276		return filepath.Join(base, projectSeg[:idx], sessionID+".jsonl")
277	}

279	// --- Transcript flush sentinel ---
280	
281	// stopHookSentinel is the string that appears in Claude Code's hook_progress
282	// entry when the stop hook has been invoked, indicating the transcript is fully flushed.
283	const stopHookSentinel = "hooks claude-code stop"
284	
285	// waitForTranscriptFlush polls the transcript file for the stop hook sentinel.
286	// Falls back silently after a timeout.
287	func waitForTranscriptFlush(ctx context.Context, transcriptPath string, hookStartTime time.Time) {
288		const (
289			maxWait      = 3 * time.Second
290			pollInterval = 50 * time.Millisecond
291			tailBytes    = 4096
292			maxSkew      = 2 * time.Second
293		)
294	
295		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "agent.claudecode")
296	
297		// Fast path: skip the poll loop when the sentinel can't possibly appear.
298		// - File doesn't exist: nothing to poll.
299		// - File is stale (unmodified for 2+ min): agent isn't running anymore.
300		//   This avoids 3s timeouts per stale "active" session (e.g., agent crashed
301		//   without firing stop hook).
302		const staleThreshold = 2 * time.Minute
303		info, err := os.Stat(transcriptPath)
304		if err != nil {
305			// Most likely the file doesn't exist; other errors (permission, etc.)
306			// would also prevent polling, so skip the wait either way.
307			return
308		}
309		fileAge := time.Since(info.ModTime())
310		if fileAge > staleThreshold {
311			logging.Debug(logCtx, "transcript file is stale, skipping sentinel wait",
312				slog.Duration("file_age", fileAge),
313			)
314			return
315		}
316	
317		deadline := time.Now().Add(maxWait)
318		for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
319			if checkStopSentinel(transcriptPath, tailBytes, hookStartTime, maxSkew) {
320				logging.Debug(logCtx, "transcript flush sentinel found",
321					slog.Duration("wait", time.Since(hookStartTime)),
322				)
323				return
324			}
325			time.Sleep(pollInterval)
326		}
327		logging.Warn(logCtx, "transcript flush sentinel not found within timeout, proceeding",
328			slog.Duration("timeout", maxWait),
329		)
330	}
331	
332	// checkStopSentinel reads the tail of the transcript file and looks for the sentinel.
333	func checkStopSentinel(path string, tailBytes int64, hookStartTime time.Time, maxSkew time.Duration) bool {
334		f, err := os.Open(path) //nolint:gosec // path comes from agent hook input
335		if err != nil {
336			return false
337		}
338		defer f.Close()
339	
340		info, err := f.Stat()
341		if err != nil {
342			return false
343		}
344		offset := info.Size() - tailBytes
345		if offset < 0 {
346			offset = 0
347		}
348		buf := make([]byte, info.Size()-offset)
349		if _, err := f.ReadAt(buf, offset); err != nil {
350			return false
351		}
352	
353		lines := strings.Split(string(buf), "\n")
354		for _, line := range lines {
355			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
356			if line == "" || !strings.Contains(line, stopHookSentinel) {
357				continue
358			}
359	
360			var entry struct {
361				Timestamp string `json:"timestamp"`
362			}
363			if json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &entry) != nil || entry.Timestamp == "" {
364				continue
365			}
366			ts, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, entry.Timestamp)
367			if err != nil {
368				ts, err = time.Parse(time.RFC3339, entry.Timestamp)
369				if err != nil {
370					continue
371				}
372			}
373			// Validate timestamp is within acceptable range:
374			// - Not too far in the past (before hook started minus skew)
375			// - Not too far in the future (after hook started plus skew)
376			lowerBound := hookStartTime.Add(-maxSkew)
377			upperBound := hookStartTime.Add(maxSkew)
378			if ts.After(lowerBound) && ts.Before(upperBound) {
379				return true
380			}
381		}
382		return false
383	}

25	// and silently bailed out. The user-visible symptom was that commits made in
26	// agent worktrees never received the Entire-Checkpoint trailer, were never
27	// condensed, and never pushed `entire/checkpoints/v1`. Status was the
28	// shortest path to a regression test for that gating decision.

I have what I need. Let me explain point 3 and give you my review.

## Point 3 explained — "session matching was strict-equal on `WorktreePath`"

Every session record on disk (`.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json`) stores a `WorktreePath` field — captured at session start, from `paths.WorktreeRoot()` at the moment `UserPromptSubmit` fires. When a commit happens, hooks call `findSessionsForWorktree(currentWorktreePath)` to figure out which session(s) should be linked to the commit.

The lookup was a strict `state.WorktreePath == worktreePath`. With Claude's worktrees feature, the two values diverge:

| moment | who fires what | path observed |
|---|---|---|
| user starts Claude in `/repo` | `UserPromptSubmit` from main worktree | session created with `WorktreePath = /repo` |
| Claude internally spawns a child process inside `/repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-x/` | the child eventually runs `git commit` | git fires `prepare-commit-msg` with CWD = `/repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-x` |
| hook calls `findSessionsForWorktree("/repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-x")` | strict equal | no match — even though the session exists in main |

Without a match, the hook logs `no active sessions` at DEBUG and quietly returns. Net effect: no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, no condensation, no metadata push. Issues 1 (`transcript_path` mismatch) and 2 (`.entire/` anchoring) had to be fixed first for the hook to even reach this layer, but on their own they wouldn't have fixed the symptom — point 3 is the last gate.

The fix in `manual_commit_session.go:150` widens lookup **one-directionally**: when the caller is in a linked worktree, also accept sessions registered against the main worktree. From main, the lookup is unchanged — otherwise a commit on main could accidentally adopt a sibling Claude session running in `.claude/worktrees/<branch>`. Two regression tests cover both directions (`_LinkedWorktreeMatchesMain`, `_MainWorktreeUnchanged`).

## Review of the branch

**Overall: in good shape.** The three fixes match their stated diagnoses, gates are tight, and tests cover both the new code paths and the boundary conditions where the widening must *not* fire.

### Strengths

- **`worktreeParentCandidate`** (`lifecycle.go:262`) — `strings.LastIndex` is the right choice and is explicitly justified in the comment; `TestWorktreeParentCandidate_MarkerInRepoRoot` locks it in. The `idx <= 0` check rejects marker-at-start. Traversal protection via `validation.ValidateAgentSessionID` happens before `filepath.Join`. Candidate must exist before being returned. Permission/IO errors pass through instead of being silently swallowed.
- **`MainWorktreeRoot`** (`paths.go:151`) — forces `--path-format=absolute` (avoids a relative-path bug class), caches per-cwd like `WorktreeRoot`, and `ClearWorktreeRootCache` clears both caches so test isolation still works.
- **`AbsPath` split** (`paths.go:202`) — `.entire/*` paths route to main, everything else stays on the linked worktree. `isEntireRelPath` is traversal-resistant. The `TestAbsPath_EntireAnchoredAtMainWorktree` test asserts both halves (main for `.entire/`, linked for `src/`) and the absolute-passthrough.
- **Widening logic** (`manual_commit_session.go:160-174`) — falls back to strict-equal if `MainWorktreeRoot` resolution fails, so the change can never make any caller worse off than before.
- **`logging.Init`** (`logger.go`) — fallback chain `MainWorktreeRoot → WorktreeRoot → "."` matches expected resilience.

### Things worth flagging

1. **Cross-worktree multi-session coupling.** With the widening in place, a commit in `.claude/worktrees/feature-x` will return *both* the linked-worktree session and the main-worktree session if both exist. `filterSessionsWithNewContent` then checks each session's *own* shadow branch (`getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)`, `manual_commit_hooks.go:1565`), so they can't accidentally claim each other's files. But if the main-worktree session has its own real content (e.g., a parallel Claude session that the user is also actively running in `/repo`), both sessions get linked under the same commit. This matches the existing multi-session model (different sessions in the same directory interleave on shadow branches), the PR just extends the boundary across worktrees. Probably fine — but worth double-checking against the `manual_commit.go` multi-session docs to confirm "different worktrees" is genuinely intended to behave the same as "same worktree, different sessions."

2. **`MainWorktreeRoot` in submodules.** Inside a submodule, `--git-common-dir` returns the submodule's `.git` dir, not the parent repo's. Parent of that is the submodule root, so `.entire/` resolves to the submodule's `.entire/`. That's almost certainly the correct behavior (submodules are independent entire-state-wise), but it's not stated anywhere and you may want a sentence in the `MainWorktreeRoot` doc clarifying it.

3. **`MainWorktreeRoot` cache invalidation on cwd changes.** Mirrors `WorktreeRoot`'s existing behavior, so consistent — but if any future code path `os.Chdir`s mid-process it'll need to call `ClearWorktreeRootCache`. Existing risk, not introduced here.

4. **Doc nit in `logging.Init` fallback** — "environments where --git-common-dir resolution fails" — in practice this also implies `WorktreeRoot` fails (not in a git repo at all), so the secondary fallback to `WorktreeRoot` is dead code. Not worth changing, but the comment slightly overstates the value of the chain.

5. **Upstream Claude limitations** are correctly called out in the PR notes (inner Claude session not firing its own `UserPromptSubmit`, `transcript_path` mismatch). Worth filing those upstream as separate issues, since they're root causes that the fallbacks here paper over.

Tests are thorough — unit (`worktreeParentCandidate`, `resolveTranscriptPath` passthrough/empty/no-marker/marker-in-root/marker-at-start/outside-base/traversal/fallback), integration (`TestClaudeCode_WorktreePathFallback`, `TestLinkedWorktree_EntireSetUpVisible`), and the targeted widening tests on both sides. You're right to push back — point #2 in the PR is overstated. The `IsSetUp` gate only checks `settings.json`. In this very repo, `settings.json` is committed (I just confirmed: `git ls-files .entire/` returns `settings.json` and `.gitignore`). So a freshly-added linked worktree gets `.entire/settings.json` checked out just like any other tracked file — and `IsSetUp` returns `true`.

The PR claim "**Every** git hook firing from inside a linked worktree saw `IsSetUpAndEnabled = false`" only holds in narrower cases:

1. **`entire enable --local`-only repos** — only `settings.local.json` exists (which is gitignored, so it never materializes in a linked worktree). `IsSetUp` would fail from main too in that case, *but* `entire status` uses a different gate that checks *both* files (`status.go:86-88`), so status passes in main but not in the linked worktree. That matches the integration test's specific symptom (`TestLinkedWorktree_EntireSetUpVisible`).
2. **Repos that gitignored `.entire/settings.json` manually.**
3. **The local file overrides `enabled: true → false` in main**, so main is "enabled" but the linked worktree (which can't see `settings.local.json`) reads only the committed value.

The fix is still load-bearing — but the *real* breakage it cures isn't usually the `IsSetUp` gate. It's:

- `.entire/logs/` is gitignored → hook log writes inside a linked worktree create an orphan `.entire/logs/` inside `.claude/worktrees/<branch>/` instead of writing to the canonical `main/.entire/logs/entire.log`. The PR commit message for `logger.go` calls this out directly: *"writes to the canonical .entire/logs/entire.log instead of spawning an orphan .entire/logs directory inside each linked worktree."*
- `.entire/settings.local.json` is gitignored → user's local overrides are invisible from linked worktrees.
- Anything written to `.entire/tmp/`, `.entire/metadata/` from a hook would split between the two trees.

So my pushback to you: the PR description blames "IsSetUpAndEnabled = false" as the dominant symptom, but that only holds for `--local`-only setups. For the much more common committed-`settings.json` repo, hooks *would* run in the linked worktree under the old code — they'd just write logs, read local-override settings, and place transient state in the wrong physical directory. Still a real bug, still worth fixing, but the framing in the PR oversells what specifically was failing.

Worth asking the author whether their repro repo was set up with `--local` (which would explain the "not set up" symptom literally), and updating the description to separate "gate fails" (narrow) from "state lands in the wrong tree" (general).

Sharp observation — yes, the `.entire/` split-state problem has affected **every** linked worktree since `git worktree` machinery existed, not just Claude's auto-created ones. Let me lay out exactly what's general vs. what's Claude-specific in this PR:

## What changed in #2 (and who it affects)

The actual code change in #2 is entirely general — nothing in it knows about Claude:

| What | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `paths.AbsPath(".entire/...")` | `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` → current worktree | `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` parent → main worktree |
| `logging.Init` log dir | current worktree | main worktree |

This affects **any** linked worktree — `git worktree add ../wt-foo`, jj's colocated worktrees, anything `--git-common-dir` recognizes. A user who manually did `git worktree add ../feat-x && cd ../feat-x && claude` would have hit the same `.entire/logs/` orphaning, the same invisible `settings.local.json` overrides, the same split metadata — and now they don't.

## What *was* broken in manual worktrees before the PR

For repos with `.entire/settings.json` committed (the common case):

- `IsSetUp` returned `true` from the manual worktree — hooks ran.
- But log writes went to `wt-foo/.entire/logs/` (gitignored, orphaned, not where you'd `tail -f`).
- `.entire/settings.local.json` was invisible — any user-local override (log_level=DEBUG, custom settings) was silently ignored.
- Transient state under `.entire/tmp/`, `.entire/metadata/` split between trees.
- This had been broken forever; nobody hit it as a *visible* breakage because nobody routinely commits agent work from a manually-created worktree.

For `entire enable --local`-only repos:
- `IsSetUp` returned `false` from the manual worktree too — `entire status` and the hook gate both saw "not set up." Also broken forever; equally invisible because nobody used both flags together.

## What *is* genuinely new in this PR

- **#1 (transcript path) is Claude-specific.** That's a bug in Claude Code itself — `transcript_path` is encoded from the worktree CWD but the file is written to the parent project dir. Doesn't affect any other agent or any manual workflow.
- **#3 (session matching widening) is Claude-specific.** It only matters when the *session* was created in one worktree (main) and the *commit* fires from a different one (the linked worktree the agent spawned). Manual `git worktree add ../wt-foo && cd ../wt-foo && claude` doesn't hit this — UserPromptSubmit fires from `wt-foo`, the commit fires from `wt-foo`, strict equality matches. The bug requires an agent that spawns a subprocess into a different worktree while keeping the parent session alive. Today, that's Claude's worktrees feature.
- **#2 is general.** Claude's worktrees feature was the *trigger* that made the long-standing bug visible (auto-creates linked worktrees, auto-commits from inside them), but the fix happens to repair manual worktrees for free.

## What the PR description gets a bit wrong

The framing — "Three independent issues conspired to make agent work in linked worktrees invisible to Entire" — bundles a general linked-worktree fix (#2) into a Claude-narrative as though it were specific to Claude. It would be more accurate to say:

> #2 is a pre-existing bug in linked-worktree support that we're fixing now because Claude's worktrees feature finally made it visible. #1 and #3 are Claude-specific.

That framing would also nudge a follow-up question worth asking: are there other places that resolve relative paths from CWD-based git roots and should switch to `MainWorktreeRoot` for `.entire/*`? The PR fixed `paths.AbsPath` and `logging.Init` — anything that does `os.ReadFile(".entire/...")` directly without going through `AbsPath` is still broken in any linked worktree.

Good question to ask, and the answer splits along the two changes (#2 vs #3) because they touch different things:

## Session data: not affected by either change

Session state has always lived in `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json`, which is anchored at `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (the **shared** .git dir). See `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_state.go:25-31`:

```go
func getSessionStateDir(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
    commonDir, err := GetGitCommonDir(ctx)  // shared, pre-existing
    ...
    return filepath.Join(commonDir, session.SessionStateDirName), nil
}
```

Same goes for shadow branches (`entire/<commit-hash>-<worktreeHash>`, in shared git refs) and the committed metadata branch (`entire/checkpoints/v1`, also shared git refs). None of that moves.

## #3 (session-matching widening) is purely additive

The widening only ADDS matches, never removes:

```
From linked worktree wt-foo (before): returns sessions where WorktreePath == wt-foo
From linked worktree wt-foo (after):  returns sessions where WorktreePath == wt-foo
                                      PLUS sessions where WorktreePath == main
```

So a user who's been working in `git worktree add ../wt-foo` and has sessions with `WorktreePath = wt-foo` — those still match strict-equal from `wt-foo` after the upgrade. Nothing is hidden. The new behavior only kicks in if there *also* happens to be a main-worktree session, which the old code couldn't see.

## #2 (`.entire/` anchoring) does silently relocate some on-disk state

This is where your concern is valid. The gitignored, filesystem-local pieces that the old code wrote into the linked worktree's `.entire/` now resolve to main's `.entire/`:

| file | impact |
|---|---|
| `wt-foo/.entire/logs/` | orphaned — still on disk but new writes go to `main/.entire/logs/` |
| `wt-foo/.entire/settings.local.json` | **silently ignored** — CLI now reads `main/.entire/settings.local.json` |
| `wt-foo/.entire/tmp/` | orphaned, transient anyway |
| `wt-foo/.entire/metadata/` | mostly an in-git-tree path concept (see `temporary.go:310` — those `EntireMetadataDir` references build git trees, not filesystem files). Light filesystem usage; whatever's there gets orphaned. |

The interesting one is `settings.local.json`. If someone deliberately had per-worktree local overrides (e.g., `wt-foo/.entire/settings.local.json` with `log_level: DEBUG` for noisy debugging of that branch), the upgrade silently swaps to main's file and they'll wonder why their overrides don't apply anymore. The PR doesn't migrate or warn about this.

## So the practical answer

- **Session continuity: safe.** Existing sessions still work from any worktree, before and after.
- **Auxiliary state: relocated.** Logs orphaned (annoying, not destructive). `settings.local.json` overrides silently swapped (user-visible behavior change). The PR doesn't mention this transition and there's no migration step.

That's a fair thing to call out on the PR — at minimum a NOTES section saying "if you had per-worktree `.entire/settings.local.json` overrides in linked worktrees, they will be ignored after this change; the canonical location is now the main worktree." Possibly a `entire doctor` check that warns when it finds an orphan `.entire/` in a linked worktree.

All four callsites checked. Three are safe; one actually fixes a latent bug.

## Callsite 1 — post-rewrite (line 210)

**Safe. No behavior change.**

```go
sessions, _ := s.findSessionsForWorktree(ctx, worktreePath)
for _, state := range sessions {
    s.remapSessionForRewrite(ctx, repo, state, rewrites)  // no-op if BaseCommit not in rewrites
}
```

`remapSessionForRewrite` is a per-session filter on `state.BaseCommit ∈ rewrites`. A rebase in a linked worktree only rewrites commits on that worktree's branch — main's session BaseCommit (pointing at main's branch HEAD) wouldn't be in the rewrites list anyway, so the old "always widen" code was just iterating over main's session for a guaranteed no-op. Removing it from the list changes nothing.

## Callsite 2 — amend trailer restore (line 582)

**Safe. New behavior is marginally better.**

```go
for _, state := range sessions {
    if state.BaseCommit != currentHead { continue }
    if state.LastCheckpointID.IsEmpty() { continue }
    // restore this session's trailer onto the amend
    return nil
}
```

Picks the first session whose `BaseCommit == HEAD` and has a `LastCheckpointID` to restore. In the both-exist case, old behavior could pick main's session and stamp an unrelated checkpoint ID onto an amend happening in the linked worktree (if main's BaseCommit happened to equal the linked worktree's HEAD). Vanishingly unlikely, but technically the new fallback-only behavior eliminates the misattribution path.

## Callsite 3 — post-commit with checkpoint trailer (line 921)

**Safe. New behavior aligns with the documented multi-session model.**

```go
for _, state := range sessions {
    s.postCommitProcessSession(..., state, ..., checkpointID, ...)
}
```

All returned sessions get bundled under the single `checkpointID` from the trailer. The CLAUDE.md docs describe multi-session as "checkpoints from different sessions **in the same directory** interleave on the same shadow branch." Different worktrees aren't the same directory, so the new behavior (only local session bundled when local exists) actually matches the documented intent better than the old "always widen" which would have cross-bundled.

The `countWarnableStaleEndedSessions` call at line 1035 is also restricted to local sessions now — main's stale ENDED sessions won't trigger a warning from a linked-worktree commit. That's fine; they'll trigger on main's next commit.

## Callsite 4 — `postCommitUpdateBaseCommitOnly` (line 1447)

**Fixes a latent bug in the current PR.**

The function's own comment says it updates BaseCommit "for **all sessions on the current worktree**" — strict equality was the original intent; widening was an unnoticed regression.

```go
for _, state := range sessions {
    if !state.Phase.IsActive() { continue }
    if state.BaseCommit != newHead {
        state.BaseCommit = newHead       // ← clobbers main's BaseCommit
        state.RealignAttributionBase(newHead)
        s.saveSessionState(ctx, state)
    }
}
```

Fires when a commit has no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. With the old "always widen" semantics, a commit in a linked worktree without a trailer would clobber main's active session BaseCommit to point at the **linked worktree's HEAD** — a commit on a different branch. That's not a no-op:

- Main's session was tracking some commit on main's branch.
- After this clobber, BaseCommit points at a commit on the linked branch.
- Main's session's shadow branch (`entire/<orig-base>-<main-worktree-id>`) is still anchored at the original commit, so the session now disagrees with its own shadow branch about what base it's working from.
- Worse: future `PrepareCommitMsg` on main has filter `BaseCommit == currentHeadHash` (the comment in this very function spells this out) — and now main's session's BaseCommit is a commit that doesn't exist on main's branch, so the session is silently skipped on main's next commit. No trailer, no condensation. Effectively kills the main session.

This is reachable in the current PR via, e.g., user manually editing the commit message in a linked worktree to remove the trailer, or any code path that creates a commit-without-trailer from a linked worktree while a main session is active. Silent and rare, but real.

The middle-ground patch eliminates this entirely — main's session is no longer in the iteration when a no-trailer linked-worktree commit fires.

## Summary

| callsite | old "always widen" | new "fallback only" |
|---|---|---|
| post-rewrite (210) | wasted no-op iteration | same outcome |
| amend trailer restore (582) | could misattribute (rare) | safer |
| post-commit w/ trailer (921) | cross-worktree bundling | matches multi-session doc intent |
| `updateBaseCommitOnly` (1447) | **could clobber main's BaseCommit, killing the session** | strict-local, correct |

So the middle-ground isn't just a cosmetic improvement — it also fixes a real (if narrow) corruption path at callsite 4 that the current PR introduced. Worth highlighting in the PR description / commit message if you carry this change forward.
